lead.title: Resilience raises €48M from PSG Equity to move beyond oncology and expand abroad
lead.deck: The €48M figure comes from French press (one version of the announcement says €40M); PSG Equity is the sole investor. The remote-monitoring platform, developed with Gustave-Roussy, tracks 37,000 patients across more than 220 facilities and supports over 20 clinical studies; funds target psychiatry, gastroenterology, new countries and possible acquisitions.

milestone.title: Estonia approves a bill allowing 24/7 robotic pharmacies with a pharmacist on video
milestone.summary: The government approved on November 5 an amendment to the medicines act: digital ID verification, video consultation with a licensed pharmacist and robotic dispensing. The bill still needs parliamentary approval, with implementation targeted for March 1, 2027.
milestone.why: If passed, it would be Europe's first authorisation of prescription dispensing without an on-site pharmacist; the law is technology-neutral, so open beyond Grab2Go, which targets a commercial rollout in March 2027.

brefsEurope.title: Nayara closes SFC Capital-led pre-seed for its AI patient companions
brefsEurope.summary: Amount undisclosed; the AI answers routine patient questions and flags concerns to clinical teams. Funds go to product, clinical validation and commercial expansion.

brefsIntl.title: Arkstone launches Arkstone Next, an AI decision-support platform for infectious disease
brefsIntl.summary: Built for sites without specialists (rural clinics, long-term care), it guides antibiotic choice, dose and duration; no regulatory status is mentioned.

word.fr: Telepharmacy: a pharmacist remotely supervises, by video, the dispensing of medicines at a site where they are not present, often via an automated unit.
word.definition: Telepharmacy lets a pharmacist review a request, advise the patient and authorise dispensing of a medicine by video link, without being physically in the pharmacy.

parts.label: Touchscreen kiosk + video
parts.role: The patient picks a medicine on a screen then talks by video with a qualified pharmacist.

parts.label: Storage and dispensing robot
parts.role: An automaton, inside a secure steel enclosure accessible only to authorised staff, stores and dispenses the boxes.

parts.label: Identity and validation
parts.role: Identity is verified (ID card or other digital solution) and the pharmacist authorises dispensing.

how.t: The customer selects medicines on a touchscreen; identity is verified by ID card or other digital solution.
A qualified remote pharmacist reviews the request and authorises dispensing.
The robot, locked in a secure enclosure, retrieves the boxes and hands them to the customer, 24/7 in the Estonian project.

word.why: VC angle: the regulator is opening a market. Estonia approved a bill on November 5, 2026 (still before Parliament, application targeted for March 1, 2027) that could make it the first European country to allow remote dispensing of prescription medicines. Grab2Go positions itself as a technology provider (hardware and software) for pharmacy operators, with a targeted 2–3 year payback for the operator; Canada, Sweden, Norway and Austria are reportedly interested. The demographic driver is real: per the cited impact study, 53% of pharmacists and 43% of pharmacy technicians are over 50. Risks: parliamentary adoption, country-by-country regulatory replicability.

startups.name: Grab2Go
startups.use: Estonian start-up supplying hardware and software for automated pharmacy with video consultation of a pharmacist; six-month pilot in Estonia with no robot malfunction reported, commercial rollout targeted for March 2027.

startups.name: Pharmacierge
startups.use: UK private e-prescription company (mPrescribe) running a robotic pharmacy in London with a multi-arm dispensing robot; over 4,500 doctor users in 2023. Adjacent to telepharmacy (remote prescribing and dispensing), not video-pharmacist.
